newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ATLETICO MADRID PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF ATLETICO MADRID PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Atletico Madrid players most likely to play in Saturday's Spanish league match against Real Madrid in the Vicente Calderon stadium:

Jose Molina, goalkeeper, age 26. One of the stars of last season's double win after signing from Albacete, Molina's characteristic sorties from the area make the Atletico offside trap difficult to beat. Came on as a striker and nearly scored on his sole international appearance in a friendly last year.
Santi Denia, defender, 22. Tough central defender who joined Atletico with Molina from Albacete last season and quickly became an ever-present in the side.
Roberto Solozabal, defender, 27. Quiet but influential, Solozabal is the unofficial leader of the Atletico defence and an automatic first-choice.
Toni Munoz, defender, 28. Toni's speed down the left and powerful shot are crucial elements in Atletico's counter-attacking strategy.
Delfi Geli, defender, 27. Quick right-sided defender who has been practically ever-present in Atletico line-ups over the past three seasons.
Daniel Prodan, defender, 24. Signed over the New Year after impressing Radomir Antic with his European Cup performances for Steaua Bucharest and scored on his league debut.
Juan Lopez, defender/midfielder, 27. Spanish international utility man who has hardly played this season. A sometimes reckless tackler, Lopez is prone to getting sent off.
Veljko Paunovic, midfielder, 20. Another Yugoslav who has caught the eye of Radomir Antic. Scored on his league debut against Zaragoza last week.
Carlos Aguilera, defender/midfielder, 27. Struggling to hold down a first-team place since rejoining Atletico from Tenerife, Aguilera is strong in joining attacks down the right.
Juan Vizcaino, midfielder, 30. Solid midfielder who provides support for creative chiefs Caminero and Pantic.
Milinko Pantic, midfielder, 30. Serbian set-piece specialist who has blossomed since signing as an unknown from Greek side Panionios last season. Suffers from too many 'off days'.
Diego Simeone, midfielder, 26. Tough Argentine international who will play only if soccer authorities overturn a suspension for a vicious challenge on Athletic Bilbao's Julen Guerrero.
Radek Bejbl, midfielder, 24. A star in the Czech Republic's Euro 96 campaign, Bejbl has had a patchy season since signing for Atletico but is likely to start the game in the absence of Simeone.
Roberto Fresnedoso, midfielder, 24. Has improved dramatically this season while filling in for Caminero. Currently combining soccer with military service in the army.

Jose Luis Caminero, midfielder, 29. Atletico's undisputed playmaker who shot to prominence in the 1994 World Cup. Caminero is fighting to get fit after injuring himself in scoring a first-minute goal in last weekend's league game.
Kiko Narvaez, striker, 24. One of the most imaginative strikers in the country, Kiko led Spain to Olympic glory in 1992. Not a great goalscorer but tends to find the mark at crucial moments.

Juan Eduardo Esnaider, striker, 23. Argentine international who helped Zaragoza to the Cup Winners' Cup in 1995 but failed to perform on his return to Real Madrid. Combines well with Kiko and Caminero but is dogged by a quick temper.
Leonardo Biagini, striker, 19. Promising young Argentine who is likely to get his chance only if Esnaider and Kiko fail.
Juan Carlos Gomez, striker, 23. Another second-line forward who has scored some valuable goals after coming on as substitute.
